cards.explanation: The answer is False. Amos says the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers (Amos 1:2). So when the LORD roars, the land feels it. Even the grass is not having a good day, and Amos is a sheepherder, so I think those pastures matter to him.

The answer is that they will be cut off. The LORD says, "I will cut off the ruler from the Valley of Aven and the one who wields the scepter in Beth-eden." (Amos 1:5) Those rulers are in charge now, and the LORD says they'll be cut off. He also says He will break down the gates of Damascus.
The answer is False. The verse says, "The people of Aram will be exiled to Kir…" says the LORD (Amos 1:5). They don't get to stay in their land. It's a heavy line, and I think it's hard to read.

The answer is that Gaza exiled them and handed them to Edom. The LORD says Gaza "…exiled a whole population, delivering them up to Edom." (Amos 1:6) Notice it's a whole population, not a few people here and there. That's why Gaza is on the list.

The answer is True. After Ekron, the LORD says, “…and the remnant of the Philistines will perish…” says the Lord GOD (Amos 1:8). A remnant is whatever's left over, and here even that is not left standing. The LORD names Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron, and then covers all the rest.

The answer is a whole congregation of exiles. The LORD says Tyre "…delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom…" (Amos 1:9) It sounds a lot like the charge against Gaza, friends. Two cities handing people over to Edom, and both are on the list.

The answer is breaking a covenant of brotherhood. The LORD says Tyre delivered up exiles to Edom "…and broke a covenant of brotherhood." (Amos 1:9) So the charge has two parts, and the second is about a covenant Tyre broke. A covenant is a serious promise, and the LORD names this one as a covenant of brotherhood.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “his anger raged continually, and his fury flamed incessantly.” (Amos 1:11) Continually and incessantly are the key words, so it didn't flare once and fade. Edom stifled all compassion, and this anger never let up either.

The answer is to enlarge their territory. The LORD says they did it "…in order to enlarge their territory." (Amos 1:13) It's one of the heaviest lines in the whole passage. I think this one hurts to read. The LORD names the reason, and it was about land.

The answer is that he will go into exile with his princes. The LORD says, "Their king will go into exile—he and his princes together," (Amos 1:15) and that's the whole picture. The ones at the top don't get a separate exit. They go together.

The answer is True. The LORD says Moab "…burned to lime the bones of Edom’s king." (Amos 2:1) It's a hard charge. It's also a reminder that Edom shows up in this passage as a nation with a charge, and also as someone who was wronged.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will cut off the ruler of Moab and kill all the officials with him…” says the LORD (Amos 2:3). So it's not only the ruler, the officials are included. The first half of the statement was true, friends, and the second half is what flips it.

The answer is law. The LORD says Judah, “…reject the Law of the LORD and fail to keep His statutes…” (Amos 2:4) So the charge isn't about another nation. It's about the LORD's own Law, and Judah is the one rejecting it.

The answer is that it goes back generations. The LORD says Judah is led astray by "…the lies in which their fathers walked." (Amos 2:4) Their fathers walked in those lies before them. This is no fresh batch, friends, it's been around for generations.
